title: Weekly Rising Savings Jar
statement:
Someone saves coins in a jar every day, starting on a Monday. The rule is:

  • On the Monday of week w (weeks are numbered from 1), they put in w coins.
  • Every other day they put in one coin more than the day before, until Sunday.

So week 1 goes 1, 2, …, 7, and week 2 starts again at 2 and goes up to 8. Return the total number of coins in the jar after n days.

examples.why: Week 1 is 1 + … + 7 = 28. Week 2 restarts at 2, so the next two days add 2 + 3.
Week 2 is 2 + … + 8 = 35. Day 15 is the Monday of week 3, which adds 3, not 9.

hints: Simulate it first: the deposit on day d (counting from 0) depends only on which week it is in and which weekday it is.
Day d is in week floor(d / 7) and is weekday d mod 7. The deposit is floor(d / 7) + 1 + (d mod 7).
A full week w adds 7w + 21. Sum that over the full weeks with the formula for 1 + 2 + … + f, then add the short last week.

explain.intuition:
Number the days from 0. Day d is in week q = ⌊d / 7⌋ (0-based) and is weekday d mod 7. The deposit is q + 1 + (d mod 7): the week's Monday amount plus one coin per day since Monday. A loop over the days is already O(n) and fast enough.

To make it O(1), group by weeks. A full week w adds w + (w+1) + … + (w+6) = 7w + 21. With f = ⌊n / 7⌋ full weeks, their total is 7·f(f+1)/2 + 21f. The leftover r = n mod 7 days start at f + 1, adding r(f+1) + r(r−1)/2.
steps: Let f = ⌊n / 7⌋ be the number of full weeks and r = n mod 7 the leftover days.
Leftover days: they start at f + 1 coins, so add r(f+1) + r(r−1)/2.
pitfalls: Letting the deposit keep rising across weeks. Each Monday drops back to the week number, as in the third example.
Mixing 0-based and 1-based week numbers: the first Monday deposit is 1, not 0.
Overflowing a 32-bit integer for large n. The total for n = 1 000 000 is about 7 · 10¹⁰.

solutions.title: Day by day
solutions.idea: Compute each day's deposit from its week and weekday, and add them up.

solutions.title: Closed form
solutions.idea: Full weeks form an arithmetic series of weekly totals; the last partial week is another short series.

followups: Given a target amount, find the first day the jar reaches it. Can you avoid simulating?
Weeks now have d days instead of 7. Generalise the formula.
